sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew (Andy). n.d. [c. 2019-2021]. 'Mangish (Mondzish)'. In: Sino-Tibetan Branches Project (STBP) by Andy Hsiu (website), Eastern Sino-Tibetan > Burmo-Qiangic > Lolo-Burmese; with a Downloads folder of comparative spreadsheets (ST branches database Hsiu2019, MSEA proto-languages database 2019-1-30).
sources.note: Nothing: the entire page body is one sentence, 'Mangish may have a non-Burmo-Qiangic substratum originating from an earlier Eastern Sino-Tibetan branch.' No phonology, no tone or stress remark; the site's Downloads are lexical comparison spreadsheets only.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2018. Classifications of some lesser-known Lolo-Burmese languages. MSEA Languages blog, December 2017, updated January 2018.
sources.note: Lexically based subgrouping notes for dozens of Loloish lects; no phonological description of Mondzish or Mango; the words tone/stress occur only in other languages' names or not at all.
sources.venue: MSEA Languages blog, December 2017, updated January 2018

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2018. Mondzish branch. MSEA Languages field-notes website (revised classification of Mondzish; cited by en/zh Wikipedia as Hsiu 2018).
sources.note: Classification and a distribution map only ('No clear internal subgrouping can be determined for the Core Mondzish languages, which is a linkage'); no phonology, no tone or stress statement for any lect.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Mango audio word list (125 wav files). Zenodo. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1123367
sources.note: The only primary data for Mango; an instrumental look at disyllables (e.g. mei55 te33, ba33 wo21) would be the only way to say anything about prominence, since no prose description exists.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Mondzish lexical database. Zenodo. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1249169 (xlsx)
sources.note: Nothing; ~430-item transcribed wordlist, column 'Mango (Mumei)', every syllable tone-marked (e.g. 'one' te53); Sources sheet: 'Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. Audio recordings.' No prose.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2015-2017. Lab notes (11) to the Experiment.com project 'Survey of Highly Endangered Mondzish Languages in Yunnan, China' (DOI 10.18258/4173), incl. 'One of the last speakers of the Mango language' (13 Jan 2015) and 'Dear project backers' (21 Dec 2017, project results).
sources.note: Nothing. The Mango note is a photo caption: 'One of the last speakers of the Mango language, which is a new language I had discovered in April 2013. Just under 50 fluent speakers remain in 2 small villages. Nearly all fluent are over 50 years old..'. The 2017 results note lists deposits for Mauphu, Mongphu, Motang, Kathu, Nasu (Lanqing) and says transcribed word lists are on msealangs/Zenodo. The words tone, tonal, stress, accent, pitch do not occur in any of the 11 notes.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new branch of Lolo-Burmese. Presentation slides, 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), Academia Sinica, Taipei, 29 pp. Second file ('') of Zenodo record DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1127814.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or the tone system. The whole deck (extracted text, 300 lines, 29 slides) contains no occurrence of tone/tonal/stress/accent/pitch/prosody; the only phonological remark about Mango is segmental ('Preserves two final stops /-t/ and /-k/, as in ʑat53 chicken and tjok53 nose'), and the 'Mondzish lexical innovations' table cites three Mango forms with Chao tone numbers (eye qhai55, ear qoŋ33, nose tjok53). Same content as sec. 2.3 of the paper already read as silent; adds nothing prosodic.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. In Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), 62-81. Taipei: Academia Sinica. Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1127814
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.3 'Mango and Manga' gives location, <50 elderly speakers, autonym ma55 ngo21, and 'Mango is the only Mondzish language that has final stops.. /-t/ and /-k/'; appendix comparative wordlist has a 'Mango (Mumei)' column with syllable tones. The words stress/accent/prosody do not occur. Only Glottolog reference for mang1429.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14)

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Survey of Highly Endangered Mondzish Languages in Yunnan, China. Experiment.com crowdfunding project report (Crossref type 'report', publisher 'Experiment', issued 2014-12-06), DOI 10.18258/4173; with 11 lab notes 2015-2017.
sources.note: No phonology content: project rationale (6 Mondzish languages, most <500 speakers, Mango <50 elderly speakers, documentation 'extremely urgent'), plan for one month of word-list/audio fieldwork, budget, lab-note titles ('Dear project backers' 2017, 'Recent progress in Southeast Asian historical linguistics' 2015, 'Travel to China for language research' 2015). Only phonological remark anywhere is about Kathu preserving kl- clusters. Nothing on tone inventory, stress or accent for Mango.
